The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team** represented **Harvard University** during the **2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season**. Coached by **Tommy Amaker** in his fifth season, the team achieved historic success, winning the **Ivy League** for the first time since **1946** and earning the program's first-ever **NCAA Tournament bid**. Here’s a detailed breakdown of the season:

---

### **Key Facts & Achievements**
- **Record**: **26–5** (12–2 Ivy League) – **Ivy League Champions**
- **NCAA Tournament**: **#12 seed** in the **West Region** (lost to #5 Vanderbilt in the First Round)
- **AP Poll**: **#25** (first-ever AP ranking for Harvard basketball)
- **Coach**: **Tommy Amaker** (5th season)
- **Home Court**: **Lavietes Pavilion** (Cambridge, MA)

---

### **Season Highlights**
1. **Historic Ivy League Title**
   - Harvard won the **Ivy League regular-season championship** for the first time in **66 years** (since 1946).
   - The Crimson secured the title with a **69–62 win over Yale** on **March 3, 2012**, finishing **12–2** in conference play.
   - They shared the title with **Princeton** (who also went 12–2) but earned the **NCAA Tournament auto-bid** due to a **head-to-head sweep** (Harvard won both meetings).

2. **First NCAA Tournament Appearance**
   - Harvard earned its **first-ever NCAA Tournament bid** in program history.
   - They were seeded **#12** in the **West Region** and faced **#5 Vanderbilt** in the **First Round** (now known as the First Four).
   - **Result**: **68–79 loss** to Vanderbilt (March 15, 2012, in Albuquerque, NM).
     - **Keith Wright** (Harvard’s star forward) led the team with **18 points**, but Vanderbilt’s size and experience proved too much.

3. **National Rankings & Recognition**
   - The Crimson entered the **AP Top 25** for the first time in program history, peaking at **#22** in February 2012.
   - They were also ranked in the **Coaches Poll** and received votes in the **RPI** (finishing **#35** in the final RPI rankings).

4. **Non-Conference Success**
   - Harvard went **14–3** in non-conference play, including:
     - A **67–62 win over Florida State** (then ranked #22) in the **Battle 4 Atlantis** (November 2011).
     - A **75–72 win over Boston College** (ACC team).
     - A **close loss to #3 Connecticut (67–68)** in the **2011 Maui Invitational**.
   - Their only other losses were to **#1 Kentucky (65–69)** and **#10 Memphis (52–60)**.

5. **Key Players & Statistics**
   - **Keith Wright (Sr., F)** – **Team leader**, **Ivy League Player of the Year (2011–12)**, averaged **16.3 PPG, 8.1 RPG, 1.8 BPG**.
     - First-team **All-Ivy** and **Academic All-American**.
   - **Oliver McNally (Sr., G)** – **10.1 PPG, 3.5 APG**, clutch shooter (hit the game-winner vs. Yale to clinch the Ivy title).
   - **Kyle Casey (Jr., F)** – **11.3 PPG, 5.5 RPG**, versatile forward.
   - **Brandyn Curry (Jr., G)** – **7.2 PPG, 4.3 APG**, steady point guard.
   - **Christian Webster (Jr., G)** – **8.8 PPG**, sharpshooter (40.3% from three).
   - **Laurent Rivard (So., G)** – **7.5 PPG**, improved three-point shooter (38.5%).
   - **Wes Saunders (Fr., G)** – **4.2 PPG**, future star (would become Ivy POY in 2014–15).

6. **Coaching & Style of Play**
   - **Tommy Amaker** implemented a **disciplined, defensive-minded system** with an emphasis on **three-point shooting** and **ball movement**.
   - Harvard ranked **#1 in the Ivy League in scoring defense (60.8 PPG allowed)** and **#2 in field goal percentage defense (39.8%)**.
   - Offensively, they relied on **Wright’s post play** and **outside shooting** (37.5% from three as a team).

7. **Notable Games**
   - **Nov. 23, 2011**: **Harvard 67, #22 Florida State 62** (Battle 4 Atlantis) – Upset win over an ACC team.
   - **Dec. 8, 2011**: **Harvard 75, Boston College 72** – Beat an ACC opponent on the road.
   - **Feb. 11, 2012**: **Harvard 59, Princeton 57** – Swept Princeton in Ivy play.
   - **March 3, 2012**: **Harvard 69, Yale 62** – Clinched the Ivy League title.
   - **March 15, 2012**: **Harvard 68, #5 Vanderbilt 79** (NCAA Tournament First Round).

8. **Postseason & Legacy**
   - The **2011–12 team** is considered the **foundation of Harvard’s basketball renaissance** under Amaker.
   - It was the first of **four straight Ivy League titles (2012–2015)** and **six NCAA Tournament appearances in eight years (2012–2015, 2017–2018)**.
   - **Keith Wright** and **Oliver McNally** became **Harvard’s first NBA Summer League players** (Wright with the Celtics, McNally with the Knicks).
   - The team’s success helped **elevate Harvard’s national profile** in basketball, leading to increased recruiting and facilities upgrades.

---

### **Statistical Leaders (2011–12)**
| Player          | PPG  | RPG  | APG  | FG%   | 3P%   | FT%   |
|-----------------|------|------|------|-------|-------|-------|
| Keith Wright    | 16.3 | 8.1  | 1.5  | 54.5% | 33.3% | 72.4% |
| Kyle Casey      | 11.3 | 5.5  | 1.2  | 50.0% | 30.0% | 68.8% |
| Oliver McNally  | 10.1 | 3.0  | 3.5  | 42.9% | 38.5% | 85.7% |
| Brandyn Curry   | 7.2  | 3.1  | 4.3  | 41.2% | 34.8% | 75.0% |
| Christian Webster | 8.8 | 2.5  | 1.4  | 40.0% | 40.3% | 80.0% |

---

### **Impact & Historical Significance**
- **First NCAA Tournament appearance** in program history (116 years after the team’s founding in 1900).
- **First Ivy League title since 1946** (a 66-year drought).
- **First AP Top 25 ranking** for Harvard basketball.
- **Laid the groundwork** for future success, including:
  - **2013–14**: First NCAA Tournament win (upset over #3 Cincinnati).
  - **2014–15**: First **NIT Final Four** appearance.
  - **2017–18**: First **NCAA Tournament win over a #6 seed (North Carolina)**.
- **Proved that Ivy League basketball could compete nationally**, paving the way for future mid-major success stories.

---

### **Where Are They Now?**
- **Keith Wright** – Played professionally in Europe (Spain, Israel, Germany) before becoming a **coach** (assistant at Harvard, then head coach at **Newbury College**).
- **Oliver McNally** – Played professionally in **Germany** before entering **private equity**.
- **Kyle Casey** – Played professionally in **Australia** and **Germany**; later worked in **finance**.
- **Brandyn Curry** – Played professionally in **Germany** and **Israel**; now works in **real estate**.
- **Christian Webster** – Played professionally in **Germany**; later became a **software engineer**.
- **Laurent Rivard** – Played professionally in **France** and **Germany**; now works in **finance**.
- **Wes Saunders** – Played professionally in **Germany** and **Australia**; later became a **venture capitalist**.
- **Tommy Amaker** – Still **Harvard’s head coach** (as of 2024), now the **winningest coach in program history**.

---

### **Fun Facts**
- The team’s **26 wins** were the **most in Harvard history** at the time (since surpassed by the 2013–14 team, which went 27–5).
- **Keith Wright** was the first **Ivy League Player of the Year** from Harvard since **1984**.
- The **2011–12 team** was featured in **ESPN’s "30 for 30" short film** *"Harvard Hoops"* (2014), documenting their historic season.
- **Jeremy Lin** (Harvard ’10) was a **student assistant coach** for the team during the 2011–12 season while recovering from injuries (before his NBA breakout with the Knicks).

---

### **Conclusion**
The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson** were a **trailblazing team** that **ended a 66-year Ivy League title drought**, made the **program’s first NCAA Tournament appearance**, and **put Harvard basketball on the national map**. Their success under **Tommy Amaker** marked the beginning of a **golden era** for Harvard hoops, inspiring future generations of players and proving that an Ivy League school could compete with power-conference programs.
